law: The workbench feature matrix is generated from the DX0 canonical exposure descriptors plus producer-registered capabilities. It replaces the manually curated compiler-demo tab list as the feature-coverage authority for the playground product; a literal hand-written feature list in workbench UI code is a coverage defect once PG2's generated explorer is the active authority.

vocabulary.dxOperationId: DX0 feature-exposure-contract.v1.json operation ids only; PG0 mints no parallel operation namespace. Each operationCoverage row must equal the joined DX0 row on hostExecutionClass, answerRail, browserExecutable and playground status, and must carry the joined promotionBlocked state (absent means not blocked).
vocabulary.workbenchState: DX0 playgroundStatus enum (exposed, partial, missing) joined verbatim from the DX0 row; PG0 never restates it independently.
vocabulary.familyStateSource: exposed: every joined DX0 operation has workbenchState exposed; partial: at least one joined operation is exposed or partial, or a preserved PG0.1 surface ships while another part of the family is uncovered; missing: every joined operation has a shipping producer but no workbench route (the family renders as blocked/pending promotion, never as success); future: no shipping producer exists anywhere yet, so the family is a registered obligation with a named producing node and renders as the distinct future state, never as successful empty output.
vocabulary.answerRail: DX0 rails-policy.v1.json rails (semantic, inspection, comparison, none); inspection-rail answers stay labelled and never substitute semantic-rail answers.
vocabulary.hostExecutionClassSource: DX0 host-execution-class.v1.json; synonymous restatements describe but never define classes
vocabulary.completenessStateSource: DX0 product-receipt-basis.v1.json completenessStates; complete-empty is a successful empty answer and every other non-complete state is distinct from it

preservedSurface.obligation: Multifile editing, Vue/Svelte outputs, preview, timings, version selection, themes and compiler options keep working on every workbench cutover; a cutover that removes one of these before its surviving route exists is a regression, not a migration.

displacedRoute.description: The hand-written allTabs list in packages/playground/src/output/Output.vue (preview, files, analysis, lint, outline, cssMatch, map, diagnostics, templateAst, cssVarFlow, depGraph, plus the ssr insert) is a manually curated compiler-demo feature list.
displacedRoute.cutoverRule: Characterize the existing user-visible tabs first, route each through its surviving producer (this matrix's featureFamilies rows), verify consumers, then remove the literal list. Inert generated-matrix adapters may land before PG2 activates; after activation no two active feature-coverage authorities may coexist.
displacedRoute.deletionPopulationThisNode: empty: PG0 is contract-only and deletes nothing; the cutover executes in PG2 with this matrix as the generated obligation source.

rules: PG0-AC1: a supported feature promoted by its producer (DX0 playground.status exposed, or promotionBlocked lifted) without a matching executable workbench matrix row fails coverage; the matrix is the coverage authority, and pg0.test.mjs joins every DX0 operation id to exactly one operationCoverage row with equality on class, rail, browserExecutable, status and promotionBlocked.

PG0-AC2: a capability with no shipping producer is future: its family row carries familyState future with a named futureProducer, its results render as the distinct future/unsupported completeness state, and it is never presented as successful empty output (complete-empty).
PG0-AC3: every supported feature has a runnable route, a source-linked result or explanation, and a replay scenario; a route that cannot be replayed is not executable coverage.

A NativeOnly operation's workbench route is explicitly selected native execution through the DX4/DX5 companion (or the BWH1-admitted browser semantic host where its build proves the closure); an inactive card, a hidden substitution engine or an unlabelled Portable stand-in are each coverage failures, not partial coverage.

PG0-AC-EXPOSURE: every operation this train exposes supplies its DX1 registration, executable playground adapter and replay case; until the DX1 explorer exists the schema and case are registered in this matrix and product promotion stays blocked on executable exposure.

PG0.4: a newly registered framework or profile acquires these obligations automatically when its descriptors register; the workbench does not implement missing framework compilers and does not replace TypeScript.
Inspection-rail results stay labelled with their own provenance and never substitute semantic-rail answers; generated coordinates are never presented as authored coordinates.

Every matrix result binds the DX0 product-receipt-basis field set, and stale-basis results (old source, old project, old engine, old worker, wrong result handle) are rejected rather than published as current.
